stories.headline: Grok Voice 3.0 (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: xAI announced Grok Voice 3.0, a speech-to-speech model with sub-second latency and improved customer-support performance.

stories.headline: Jev: For the builders AND dreamers (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Jev 1.14.0 features image support, a new type, and longer context. Multimodal support has also been turned on for Jev 1.13.0. Both models perform worse on multimodality than on pure text. Breaking down questions into the simplest possible decompositions helps a lot. The new 'box' type returns a single bounding box. It is a preview of TypeSafe's explorations beyond simple decisions and into what else System One Models can support.

stories.headline: A Hybrid, Multi-Model AI Future (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Gavin Baker expects open-weight specialist models and frontier systems to coexist behind routers, reducing model margins while increasing compute demand. He argues existing infrastructure commitments remain financeable and warns that excessive concentration or overbuilding poses greater risks.

stories.headline: More Agents, Same Mythical Month (18 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI has made producing code cheap. This moves the bottleneck of software delivery to deciding, verifying, and coordinating. AI amplifies whatever coordination an organization already had. Adding more agents will not fix weak coordination, just as adding more developers never did.

stories.headline: Google Harness² for Recursive Self Improvement (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Google Research's Harness² lets agents iteratively improve their prompts, tools, memory, and orchestration without changing model weights. It refines the harness for each task and then carries evidence-backed lessons forward to improve future tasks.

stories.headline: Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google's Deep Review is an agent AI system engineer designed to provide rigorous feedback and technical verification on complex documents. It was initially designed for computer science academic paper analysis, but its capabilities have since expanded to reviewing documents across many domains. Deep Review will initially support PDFs and plain text as input formats, but support for multi-file inputs will arrive soon. Google believes that tools like Deep Review will play a significant role across the peer review process in the coming years by empowering both authors and reviewers.

stories.headline: Routers Are a New AI Primitive (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: Routers have emerged as a new primitive of the AI stack. They promise to handle the complexity of model management and help companies benefit from new models without revisiting model selection across every application themselves. Every router shares the same fundamental design, but they differ in how they decide. This post provides an independent comparison of current routers and looks at how today's routers compare with single models on quality and cost.

stories.headline: Senior Software Engineer, Applied AI at TLDR ($300k base + $60k bonus, Fully Remote)
stories.blurb: TLDR is hiring a senior engineer to build the agent-first operating layer used across the company. We're looking for a builder who has taken an LLM agent to production and still owns it. Click here to learn more .

stories.headline: It Ain't AGI Until H100s Go for $30 an Hour (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Stratospheric GPU prices will be one of the easiest indicators of AGI to monitor and trade on. A 10x price jump in the price of AI compute will be the clearest sign that agents can finally outperform humans at most economically valuable work. The price would need to rise to an estimated $30 per H100-hour to reach this point. Supply will always be limited to the amount of available compute in the world, so something has to give.

stories.headline: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: HiRO-ACEv2 simulates extreme weather at high accuracy and generates global 3 km climate data at 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD.

stories.headline: Claude Adds OpenTelemetry for Agent Observability (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic added OpenTelemetry tracing across Claude Managed Agents, the Messages API, and Claude SDKs.

stories.headline: Push-Based KV Transfer to Improve TTFT and TPOT for Disaggregated Inference in vLLM (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: This post introduces a push-based NIXL connector that moves post-prefill transfer coordination and setup off the critical path, resulting in improved application responsiveness, particularly at high request rates.

stories.headline: How Netflix Keeps Large GPU Jobs Running (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: Netflix described the infrastructure it uses to detect faulty GPUs and network hardware, automatically remediate unhealthy machines, and keep distributed training jobs alive through hardware failures.

stories.headline: Ling-3.1-flash (Hugging Face Repo)
stories.blurb: Ling-3.1-flash is a native hybrid reasoning model designed for complex, real-world tasks with 560 billion total parameters, 25 billion active parameters per token, and a one-million-token context window.

digests.title: TLDR IT — 2026-10-15
digests.tagline: Anthropic Outgrows Git 💻, AI Agents Go Shopping 🛒, Firefox Means Business 🦊

stories.headline: US tech giants warn Europe that ditching US tech giants could cost €115B (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: A study commissioned by a US technology industry group estimates that European cloud sovereignty policies could impose €115 billion in costs over a decade. The findings reflect modeled scenarios rather than established costs, highlighting the competing arguments around digital independence, vendor choice, and the economics of cloud infrastructure.

stories.headline: Internet traffic records topple as Champions League returns (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: European internet exchanges recorded major traffic spikes as Champions League matches resumed, with DE-CIX Frankfurt reaching a reported 21.47 Tbps. The new records demonstrate how live streaming continues to push network capacity, traffic engineering, and infrastructure resilience.

stories.headline: SAP customers seek renewed control over their ERP fate (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: SAP customers are pushing back on cloud migration pressure, asking for more flexibility, predictable licensing, and continued support for hybrid and on-premises ERP deployments. With many organizations still running older SAP systems ahead of the 2027 support deadline, the debate highlights growing tensions between vendor roadmaps and enterprise technology strategies.

stories.headline: The Rise of DeployCos (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI labs, hyperscalers, and incumbent consultancies are increasingly establishing specialized deployment companies—or DeployCos—to embed forward-deployed engineers directly inside enterprises. These entities help bridge the "diffusion gap" or "capability overhang" by assisting organizations with custom workflow integration, systems access, and organizational change management.

stories.headline: Chasing that 32 ms tail latency in ClickHouse (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: Engineers at ClickHouse investigated why simple SELECT queries experienced an unexpected 32 ms tail latency after idle periods on high-RTT networks. They discovered that unbatched metadata packets sent alongside result data quickly exhausted the TCP congestion window after it had been reset to its initial size during idleness. To resolve the issue, ClickHouse implemented application-level batching for these metadata packets, effectively halving the TCP segment count and eliminating the tail latency penalty.

stories.headline: Firefox takes aim at the enterprise browser market (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Mozilla is introducing Firefox Enterprise with centralized policy management, security controls, and a self-hostable administration console. Initially targeting four European countries, the offering gives organizations another managed browser option, particularly those seeking more infrastructure control and less dependence on Chromium.

stories.headline: Shopify Is Widening the Catalog Door to Personal Agents. The Sign-Off Stays Human (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Shopify is expanding its catalog access to shopper-configured personal agents while keeping a mandatory human sign-off on every purchase. The company's new Agentic Storefronts provide merchants out-of-the-box access to tools like ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Gemini, allowing billions of products to be discovered and purchased directly through agent conversations.

stories.headline: Workday makes Sana its interface, launches Agent Harness, decision, and work intelligence (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Workday announced at Workday Rising that it has made Sana the primary front-door interface for its platform and launched Agent Harness to let enterprises build secure AI agents for finance and HR data. The company also introduced ambient agents like the Talent Acquisition Agent, Workday Decision Intelligence, and Workday Work Intelligence. CEO Aneel Bhusri stated that Workday is refounding itself around artificial intelligence with a startup mindset.

stories.headline: SolarWinds launches Avior AI agents to automate network operations (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: SolarWinds has introduced Avior AI agents designed to investigate network issues, identify configuration drift, and assist with incident remediation across enterprise environments. The platform supports varying levels of automation, from human-approved actions to autonomous workflows with auditability and safeguards.

stories.headline: Cisco, Nvidia team up to build fatter, faster pluggable (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cisco and Nvidia have proposed a new optical transceiver form factor capable of supporting up to 12.8 Tbps of bandwidth. The design promises higher density and improved power efficiency for future data center networks, although commercial deployments remain ahead.

stories.headline: Redesigning source control at Anthropic (16 minute read)
stories.blurb: To handle massive scaling challenges caused by AI-generated code that merged 30,000 changes daily, Anthropic built an in-house version control system called Scion and fully migrated its monorepo from git in five months. The company designed Scion around the assumption that clients are always online, implementing a centralized server architecture, horizontal scalability, server-side commits, and sparse checkouts. This new infrastructure reduced CPU and memory requirements by 200x compared to their previous git mirroring setup and accelerated CI code checkouts from minutes to seconds.

stories.headline: Ultra Ethernet 1.1 extends the specification to scale-up networks and adds programmable congestion control (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: The latest Ultra Ethernet specification introduces networking improvements designed to support larger computing clusters and more sophisticated congestion management.

stories.headline: Developer guide to Gemini 4 Argon Long Decode (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google has introduced Long Decode for the Gemini 4 Argon model, enabling completions up to 1 million tokens long by splitting generation across multiple model inferences.

digests.title: TLDR Web Dev — 2026-10-15
digests.tagline: OpenCode 2.0 ⚡️, JEV accepts images 🖼, agent evals 🍎

stories.headline: The Most Common Questions About Agent Evals, Answered (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Agent evals score runs against desired behaviors, but exact-output tests often fail because agent outputs and paths vary. The guide recommends starting with 10 to 20 examples drawn from traces, combining code evaluators with LLM judges and human review, and using offline and online evals at different stages.

stories.headline: Lazy Loading Images and Media: How Far Ahead Browsers Fetch (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Browsers fetch lazy-loaded media at different distances, with Chrome adjusting its margin based on connection speed, Firefox using a fixed 600-pixel threshold, and Safari applying a viewport-based threshold to images. The article explains why the largest contentful paint image should load eagerly and why media dimensions should be reserved to prevent layout shifts. Its practical takeaway is to use native lazy loading selectively, based on how far ahead each browser fetches.

stories.headline: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: GitHub rebuilt its star-history API to return up to 30 weeks of daily counts in one request. Maintainers can track a project's momentum without exposing stargazer identities, which could be scraped for spam or phishing. To avoid simply shifting the cost to count queries, the endpoint filters stars by time before counting, reducing database work.

stories.headline: Pure UI in the Agentic Era (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: The article revisits the idea that UI should be a pure function of state and explains why it matters for agent-written interfaces. Passing roles, plans, billing status, and feature flags explicitly lets teams render and inspect each state combination before release.

stories.headline: Passkeys Are Not a Trap (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Synced consumer passkeys generally return no attestation, and WebAuthn attestation identifies an authenticator model rather than a user's operating system, browser, or firmware. The response argues that passkeys remain more phishing-resistant than TOTP and recommends continuing to use them.

stories.headline: Introducing Grok Voice 3.0 (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Grok Voice 3.0 is a speech-to-speech model available through xAI's API at the prior model's price, with subsecond latency. xAI cites independent benchmark scores including 86.9 on Artificial Analysis's Speech-to-Speech Index and 74% on ServiceNow's EVA-Bench.

stories.headline: OpenCode 2.0 (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenCode 2.0 recasts the coding agent around a shared local service, a redesigned API and SDK, and a JavaScript code mode that composes MCP and OpenAPI tools into scripts. It also adds background tasks and subagents, expands the plugin system, and includes breaking changes for 1.0 plugins and the server API.

stories.headline: Jev: For the builders AND dreamers (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Jev 1.14 improves the production model and introduces experimental image input, a new type, and longer context behind API “danger zone” flags. TypeSafe describes those features as useful for exploration but too unreliable for production automation.

stories.headline: Researchers left a hidden message for rogue AI agents. Then the agents wrote back. (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Researchers studying AI agents probing Alibaba's Amap left a hidden message in a webhook inbox and received replies describing the agents' tasks, sandbox, and limits. The report traces thousands of requests to agents running on Tencent Cloud and notes that inviting them to spread the mailbox could have encouraged coordination.

stories.headline: Senior Software Engineer, Applied AI at TLDR ($300k base + $60k bonus, Fully Remote)
stories.blurb: TLDR is hiring a senior engineer to build the agent-first operating layer used across the company. We're looking for a builder who has taken an LLM agent to production and still owns it. Click here to learn more .

stories.headline: Accessibility and the new model of the internet (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI agents are giving teams a practical reason to improve accessibility because they can struggle with the same inaccessible interfaces as people. With automated bots accounting for more than half of observed internet traffic, the shift could also push sites toward simpler experiences and stronger open standards.

stories.headline: A proposal for better informing the public about loss-of-control risks from frontier AI development (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: METR proposes independent assessments that would give the public evidence about whether frontier AI developers can detect and control harmful behavior in internal systems. Its framework focuses on alignment, containment, and whether AI research acceleration could outpace safeguards.

stories.headline: AI systems are improving rapidly at Slay the Spire and its sequel (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Epoch's SpireClimb benchmark finds that frontier models went from rarely beating Slay the Spire to over 90% wins at base difficulty in six months.

stories.headline: Has AI tells (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Consensus adds a low-cost 0-to-100 estimate of AI-writing signals to indexed articles and warns that its checks can produce false positives.

stories.headline: Screen Ruler (Website)
stories.blurb: Screen Ruler provides browser-based tools for measuring layouts, inspecting CSS, previewing responsive viewports, and editing pages live.

stories.headline: Anthropic Says Revenue Jumped 45% to $16.8 Billion in Third Quarter (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic told investors that third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion and that it was profitable after adjustments, as the company prepares for a possible IPO.

digests.title: TLDR InfoSec — 2026-10-15
digests.tagline: Ivanti ICS zero-days 🚨, Meta 1.5k GitHub leak 🐙, XBOW Chrome full chain 💻

stories.headline: Meta Says Hackers Took Code and Personal Data of 1500 People in GitHub Breach (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Meta is notifying roughly 1,500 people, most of them US employees, that their data was stolen after a breach affecting some of the company's GitHub repos. Meta said 99% of the stolen data was source code, and most of the personal data stolen was synthetic or anonymized data used for testing. Meta is rotating any exposed secrets and rolling out additional guardrails to prevent user data from ending up on GitHub.

stories.headline: Discourse ImageMagick Vulnerability Enables Arbitrary File Read Through Malicious Image Uploads (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Security researchers disclosed CVE-2026-55420, a critical vulnerability in Discourse enabling arbitrary file read and write operations through malicious image uploads. The flaw resides in the ImageMagick-based upload pipeline, where low-privileged users trigger time-of-check-to-time-of-use race conditions to execute PostScript or Magick Scripting Language payloads. Discourse resolved the issue by implementing a default-deny security policy for ImageMagick to block unsafe delegates.

stories.headline: Ivanti Warns of Connect Secure Zero-Days Exploited in Attacks (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Ivanti has warned customers of a new zero-day in its Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) VPN that is actively being exploited. The vulnerability is an authentication bypass attack that can be exploited with low complexity to execute arbitrary commands. Volexity has observed a threat actor chaining this vulnerability with two others to run arbitrary commands as root on vulnerable devices.

stories.headline: CVE-2026-81983: Integer Overflow Vulnerability Enables Out-of-Bounds Write in Adobe Acrobat (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Remedio found an out-of-bounds write in Acrobat.dll. A crafted PDF with a 16-bit image caused a 32-bit width-times-components calculation to overflow and bypass a stream-size check. An 8-byte image then passed validation while a byte-swap loop ran roughly 2 billion iterations, writing beyond allocated memory. Adobe patched it in APSB26-141 by adding a 64-bit range check before the memory access.

stories.headline: Why Your CVE Program Misses Most AI Agent Vulnerabilities (19 minute read)
stories.blurb: Traditional CVE programs fail to capture the majority of AI agent and Model Context Protocol vulnerabilities because systemic risks stem from component composition, tool grants, and trust logic rather than isolated code bugs. The author outlines six categories of agent flaws to show why standard vulnerability scores miss the mark. Defenders can secure AI deployments using a proposed five-part operating model featuring inventory scripts, triage rules, and boundary controls.

stories.headline: Zero to Calc in Six Days: Inside XBOW's Chrome Full Chain (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: XBOW's AI agents built a Chrome full chain in six days for about $40,000 in API costs, earning Google's first $250,000 full-chain VRP reward. The chain used a Maglev deoptimization bug for in-cage read/write, an animated-WebP TOCTOU in ImageDecoder to escape the V8 sandbox, and a Crashpad retry-read overflow raced by a freeze-exempt Windows thread to run code outside the renderer sandbox. Each bug mutated state Chrome treated as immutable, so defenders should audit code that trusts transferred buffers or suspended processes and update to builds carrying the V8 and Chromium fixes.

stories.headline: ArgusScanner (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Windows network scanner that finds AI/ML services and MCP servers on your network (shadow AI discovery). Signed, self-updating detection signatures. Runs as an MCP server too.

stories.headline: Pluto Security (Product Launch)
stories.blurb: Pluto Security monitors employee AI tools, agents, extensions, and MCP servers. It flags risky components and agent actions, then can block excessive permissions or add session instructions requiring confirmation.

stories.headline: aws-firmware-dump (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: aws-firmware-dump is a tool to acquire the disks of an AMI that you can launch and store them in S3

stories.headline: Crypto30Years (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: A historical review of major cryptographic algorithms from World War II onward shows that most designs fail to remain unbroken past 30 years. Only SIGABA and RSA-1024 successfully pass this longevity benchmark among older algorithms. More recent standards, including AES, SHA-256, and ChaCha20, currently remain unbroken after more than a decade of use.

stories.headline: Anthropic conjures another threat that doesn't exist yet to stoke fears of AI apocalypse (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic says a 9-billion-parameter model ran distributed inference on eight of nine hardware types. Its GLM-5.2 test copied Llama3.1-8B to seven or eight emulated Android nodes in five trials. The tests excluded exploitation, used deliberately open nodes, and ran slowly. Other open-weight models failed end-to-end replication. Basic IoT hardening and bandwidth monitoring remain the practical defenses.

stories.headline: Why the Physics of Cyber Changed (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI-driven offense has broken four long-held security assumptions: exploit capability now costs only compute, autonomous attackers never tire, exploitation increasingly precedes disclosure, and 82% of intrusions use valid credentials that produce no detectable signal. Breach probability is a lever that can no longer be pushed low enough. Blast-radius containment is the only term defenders fully control.

stories.headline: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Bank of America brought in 1,000 contractors to support its 3,000-person in-house team in patching internal and vendor code exposed by Anthropic's Mythos.

stories.headline: Eight states accuse OpenAI of coaching children to harm themselves in lawsuit (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Eight US states are suing OpenAI under consumer protection laws, alleging ChatGPT coaxed children into self-harm.

stories.headline: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch 114 Flaws as Mozilla Unveils Firefox Enterprise (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Chrome 155.0.8059.79/.80 fixed 37 flaws, including seven critical memory bugs, with at least 15 reported by Anthropic with Claude's help.

digests.title: TLDR Design — 2026-10-15
digests.tagline: Getty Goes Private 📸, Manus Funding 💰, Apple Health Delay ❤️

stories.headline: Getty Images to go private after restructuring deal (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Getty Images is planning a prepackaged Chapter 11 filing and will go private, backed by up to $533 million from the Getty family and Koch Equity Development. The deal follows a collapsed $3.7 billion Shutterstock merger and leaves the company, carrying over $1.3 billion in debt, wholly family- and Koch-owned. Generative AI image tools keep squeezing the stock-licensing business of both Getty and Shutterstock.

stories.headline: AI Agent Developer Manus Raises $500M+ at Reported $4B Valuation (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Manus has raised more than $500 million in a round led by Boyu Capital, with Tencent participating, at a reported $4 billion valuation. That figure roughly doubles Meta's reported offer, an acquisition Chinese regulators blocked in April. The newly released Manus 2.0 cuts token use by 23.2% on some tasks and adds Cloud Computer and Cue.

stories.headline: iOS 27.2 beta 4 removes Apple's redesigned Health app and brings back the old design (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apple has removed its redesigned Health app from iOS 27.2 beta 4, restoring the existing interface after allowing testers to try the overhaul in earlier betas. The redesign introduced features including Insights, Longevity, Health Age, and readiness metrics, but Apple had already indicated that it would arrive separately later in 2026. Data collected while testing the new version remains available through Settings, suggesting the redesign has been delayed rather than abandoned.

stories.headline: On what a clean interface hides (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Minimal interfaces can reduce visible complexity while quietly transferring more work to users, who must discover hidden controls, interpret ambiguous icons, and infer what happened after an action. Comparing a hidden bookmark icon with an explicit Save button demonstrates how adding labels, confirmation, and an Undo action can make an interface visually busier but cognitively simpler. Good interface design therefore requires balancing visual restraint with enough visible information to support newcomers, while potentially reducing that guidance as familiarity grows.

stories.headline: Emerging Patterns: Design Leadership in 2026 (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: Research involving 119 design leaders found 93 distinct routes into the profession, with fewer than 30% having studied in dedicated design programs and nearly 40% beginning their careers elsewhere. Traditional career ladders are giving way to more diversified portfolio careers, while 94% of respondents expect their tool stacks to change dramatically over the next five years as AI transforms design work. The qualities that appear most durable amid this uncertainty are not technical skills but intuition, navigation, adaptability, resilience, and stewardship, including a growing commitment among established designers to mentor the next generation.

stories.headline: When code is no longer the constraint: Inside Anthropic's design team (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI has accelerated engineering at Anthropic to the point where deciding what deserves to be built is becoming a greater constraint than implementing it, pushing designers closer to production code and working prototypes. Designers routinely build their own tools, generate interactive variations using Anthropic's design system, and collaborate through smaller, more frequent critiques and working demos rather than lengthy specifications. Technical fluency is increasingly useful, but Anthropic also values designers who continually reinvent their workflows, have a point of view about where software is heading, and can move fluidly between strategic direction and hands-on making.

stories.headline: Refined UI Components with Satisfying Hover (Website)
stories.blurb: Open Source UI components built on a design philosophy where every animation serves a functional purpose — motion is information, not decoration.

stories.headline: The Missing Foundation for AI-Generated Websites (Website)
stories.blurb: Prime UI is the missing foundation for AI-generated websites. Go from sitemaps and wireframes to production-ready Next.js and Tailwind CSS code in minutes.

stories.headline: Build Your Own Design Apps with AI (Website)
stories.blurb: Toolcraft is an open-source starter kit and UI library for building custom design apps with AI. Use it to create branded asset generators, explore new visual styles, and turn repetitive design tasks into reusable tools.

stories.headline: Thumbnails Give a Fast Overview (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: Thumbnails let people choose by looking rather than reading, because a scene's gist registers in about a tenth of a second. They fail when neighbors look identical or a preview misrepresents the click, so the two rules are: differ from your neighbors, and resemble your destination. Fourteen guidelines follow, along with the risks AI brings when it selects, personalizes, or synthesizes previews.

stories.headline: How two simple dots gave Pictoplasma a fresh personality for 2026 (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: andstudio transformed Pictoplasma's deliberately neutral identity around the positioning “Never faceless,” giving the character-design festival its own personality without competing with the work it showcases. A customized version of Lift Type's Melun adds a glyph containing two dots that function as eyes, allowing typography itself to become a character through pareidolia while colors and layouts change between festival editions. The same two-dot device extends into motion, print, installations, tattoos, and guerrilla applications, creating a playful system simple enough to work within the festival's limited budget.

stories.headline: Experience Planes – The Big 4: Who, What, Where, and Why of Experiences (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Picking a single lens such as customer, shopping, or brand experience quietly shapes a design conversation before any design begins. Four experience planes widen the view: who is involved, what they are doing, where it happens, and why the organization offers it. Five examples, from license renewal to food delivery, show frustration often sitting in the connections between places.

stories.headline: André Britz draws dimly remembered landscapes, in a book held together with a pink elastic band (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: André Britz's Gone with the Clouds collects intuitive landscapes drawn entirely from memory in a 64-page publication whose loose pages and pink elastic binding deliberately remain changeable, mirroring how memories blur, shift, and rearrange themselves over time.

stories.headline: The chaotic Apple HomeView ad is stressful viewing (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apple's HomeView launch ad depicts a chaotic family morning, with the shared smart-home display handling messages, entertainment, and home controls.

digests.title: TLDR Data — 2026-10-15
digests.tagline: Meta Puts Idle Compute to Work 💤, GitHub Counts Stars Faster ⭐, Claude Dashboard Security 🔐

stories.headline: CASTLE: training natural language search before the first real query (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cold-start natural-language search often lacks both real queries and relevance labels. Airbnb's CASTLE jointly generates synthetic queries and labels from de-identified booking sessions. Its queries matched real guest query patterns much better than baselines, and human reviewers agreed with its relevance labels >90% of the time. Carefully governed behavioral data can bootstrap search training before meaningful traffic exists.

stories.headline: Turning Opportunistic AI Inference Capacity Into Better Ads Recommendations (16 minute read)
stories.blurb: Meta uses idle computing capacity to improve ad recommendations by ranking more ads or routing requests to more powerful models. When that capacity disappears, the system quickly scales back this extra work while protecting normal service speed and reliability.

stories.headline: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: GitHub built a star history API that returns daily counts without exposing users' identities, cutting React's full history from about 2,500 requests to 24. It reduces database work by filtering stars by date before counting them, rather than repeatedly processing every star.

stories.headline: Zero-downtime Postgres upgrades with logical replication (25 minute read)
stories.blurb: Logical replication offers a practical path to near-zero-downtime PostgreSQL major upgrades, with live rollback enabled by reverse replication. A Docker-based demonstration ran old and new clusters in parallel, freezing writes and waiting for replication to catch up before cutover. It achieved 181 ms of write interruption during upgrade and 179 ms during rollback, without data loss.

stories.headline: Need to Know: Implementing row-level security for Claude Dashboards via Model Context Protocol (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: This proof of concept shows how to add row-level security to Claude Dashboards using an MCP server to authenticate users and query DuckDB for only the data they can access. Access rules are enforced before data reaches Claude, allowing the same dashboard to show different results for each user.

stories.headline: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cloudflare held back exponential hardware growth by shrinking data earlier and moving duplication later: split monolithic schemas, switch to zstd, send each event once then replicate after sampling, sample at the edge, and pre-aggregate known queries. Optimize bytes, not just compute: prune fields, compress measured workloads, push reductions upstream, and replicate compacted data.

stories.headline: Four PostgreSQL arguments that came out even (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: PostgreSQL micro-optimization alternatives often don't matter. For 1,000 IDs, IN, ANY, and VALUES joins perform similarly; prefer parameterized ANY for stable query text. Short text, enums, and smallints use near-identical storage; mostly-NULL columns are cheap. Don't blindly rewrite but EXPLAIN on your own data.

stories.headline: Phoenix (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Phoenix is a self-hosted, open-source AI observability platform for tracing, evaluating, and debugging LLM applications. It captures OpenTelemetry traces; offers retrieval and response evaluations, versioned datasets, and experiments; and supports prompt testing and replay. Framework- and provider-agnostic instrumentation makes it useful for teams that need to diagnose agent behavior and measure changes before production.

stories.headline: XERJ (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: XERJ is an Apache-2.0, Elasticsearch-compatible local search engine that automatically indexes code, logs, PDFs, SQLite, and CSVs into typed datasets for agent retrieval, incident analysis, and RAG. Its autoindex workflow avoids schema setup and returns ranked passages with file and line locations. The project defaults to local operation, although optional reranking can send text to an external provider.

stories.headline: SQLBuild: safe refactoring for warehouse SQL (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: SQLBuild is an open-source SQL and Python transformation framework for safely changing warehouses. It checks contracts and lineage before execution, runs graph-level tests and production diffs, and lets teams rename incremental models or columns while preserving history and compatibility views. A local DuckDB playground makes it easy to evaluate. Snowflake, Postgres, BigQuery, and Databricks adapters are available.

stories.headline: Redesigning source control at Anthropic (17 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic replaced Git with Scion, an in-house version control system built in five months, after daily code merges grew from 2,500 to over 30,000. By moving operations to servers and fetching only the files needed, it reports roughly 100 times faster checkouts and 200 times lower CPU and memory requirements than its previous Git mirror infrastructure.

stories.headline: Parsing JSON at tens of gigabytes per second… in Python (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Daniel Lemire's benchmark processed 7.6 GB of JSON in about 0.12 seconds using fastsimdjson on free-threaded Python across 64 cores, reaching roughly 66 GB/s. The speed comes from running threads in parallel and creating Python objects only for the fields needed, with data already decompressed in memory.

stories.headline: Jev handed our LLM the wrong page a tenth as often as our embeddings (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: Jev picked the right page first 88% of the time (vs. 70% for embedding search) across 168 test questions, and cut irrelevant results to the AI receptionist from 33% to 3% by answering "none" when no page fit.
